text:
andrea: Heads-up: public advisory for FlashAttention kernels + protobuf CVE just landed. CVE-2026-12345. Vendor says exploit requires local access but PoC is circulating. Need a quick patch plan.

devon: Link?

andrea: https://security.vendor/adv/CVE-2026-12345 and a PoC gist floating around. Reproduces with triton + vLLM in our container images.

sam: If exploit needs local access, risk to hosted API is lower, but Dedicated and Private deployments could be targeted. We should triage and patch ASAP.

maria: Can we confirm our images include the vulnerable FlashAttention build? Quick grep or package list should show it.

sam: Quick check: our latest inference image `redwood/inference:2026-02-12` ships flash-attn v1.4.2 which is listed in the advisory as affected.

devon: Priority: HIGH for Dedicated/Private, MEDIUM for hosted. Recommend patch -> rebuild -> canary. Also bump protobuf; separate CVE-2026-54321 affects 3.19.x series.

andrea: Action items (rough):
  1) Upgrade flash-attn to vendor fixed release (1.4.3)
  2) Bump protobuf to patched release (>=3.22.1)
  3) Rebuild inference images (cpu/gpu/quant) and run full smoke/integration tests
  4) RBAC change: restrict runtime-exec to ops during rollout and enable stricter podSecurity for private customers
  5) Enable audit logging for package installs and container execs for the next 7 days
  6) KMS rotation: not automatically required but review if any ephemeral keys were exposed

ryan: Quick note: CVE writeup says no remote RCE without local privileges. KMS root key rotation is heavy-handed — don't rotate unless we see suspicious access. Rotate ephemeral deploy keys and rotate any leaked service account tokens.

sam: Time estimate: rebuild + CI per variant ~45 minutes. We have 3 variants -> ~2.5h total including smoke tests and push. Canary rollout window ~30-60m.

maria: I'll coordinate the canary in us-west1 on a low-traffic pool. Need a rollback hook and feature flag to force old runtime if issues.

andrea: Rollout plan suggestion: canary 5% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m with automated error budget rollback. Notify Dedicated customers with a 1h maintenance window.

devon: Checklist for builders:
```
./scripts/rebuild.sh --image redwood/inference:fix-CVE-2026-12345
# run unit & integration
./infra/smoke_tests/run.sh --target canary
kubectl apply -f k8s/rollout/canary.yaml --record
```
Add dependency updates to infra repo and pin digests.

sam: SRE oncall @ryan please approve emergency maintenance window for Dedicated customers with SLAs. We should also trigger support playbook for customer notifications.

ryan: Approved. Mark as emergency patch. I'll open a customer-facing banner draft and runbook for CS to use.

deploy-bot: Image pushed: `redwood/inference:fix-CVE-2026-12345` -> registry digest sha256:abc123def456.

maria: :thumbsup: Starting canary now (5% traffic). Monitoring dashboards: latency, 5xx, model correctness tests.

andrea: I'll update the internal advisory and post an incident-notice draft for exec review. Ping me in 30m with canary status.

devon: Post-mortem items to capture: dependency pinning policy, faster rebuild pipelines, and improving packaging isolation so kernel-level libs can't be swapped at runtime.

sam: Also add automated dependency CVE watchdog to PRs for inference images. If PoC becomes weaponized we'll escalate CVSS and notify vendors.

andrea: Thanks folks — please add short replies here with status updates.

maria: Canary stable at +10m, no regressions. Continuing 50% ramp.

ryan: Noted. CS banner sent to affected Dedicated customers.

andrea: Closing loop after full rollout. Will file follow-up ticket to audit RBAC changes and keep audit logs for 90 days.
